title: Dress Codes Decoded
short: Social dress codes run from white tie and black tie to cocktail, smart casual and casual; at work, from business formal to business casual and casual. When unsure, ask the host.
trouble: Learners read "black tie optional" as "jeans are fine" or "business casual" as athletic wear. Dressing for the occasion is a way of showing respect for the host.

blocks.html: After an interview, you will meet dress codes at work and at weddings, parties and dinners. The words can sound like a secret language, but each one names a step on a ladder from most to least formal.
Social dress codes run from white tie and black tie to cocktail, smart casual and casual. At work they run from business formal to business casual and casual. When unsure, ask the host.

A dress code helps guests feel comfortable, because no one wants to be the only person in jeans at a black-tie dinner, or the only one in a tuxedo at a picnic. Dressing for the occasion is also a way of showing respect for the host, who has planned an event of a certain kind. Since the terms are not always clear, asking is always polite.

head: Code
What it usually means
rows: The most formal: tailcoats, floor-length gowns. Rare today.
Tuxedos; formal gowns or elegant cocktail dresses.
A tuxedo or a dark suit and tie; a formal or cocktail dress.
A suit, a dress or dressy separates.
Neat and polished: slacks or nice jeans with a collared shirt or blouse, a blazer optional.
Everyday clean clothes suited to the place.
blocks.cap: Social dress codes, from most to least formal.

head: Work code
What it usually means
rows: A suit and tie, or a suit or dress with a jacket.
Slacks or a skirt with a collared shirt, blouse or sweater; no athletic wear.
Neat everyday clothes; the workplace's own norms decide.

blocks.title: Black tie optional
blocks.q: Omar's wedding invitation says "black tie optional." He doesn't own a tuxedo. What can he wear?
steps: Optional means a tuxedo is welcome but not required.
A dark suit and tie is right.

blocks.title: Business casual
blocks.q: On her first day, Mia's office is business casual. Is a hoodie and running shoes all right?
steps: Business casual is a step below a suit, not athletic wear.
Slacks or a skirt with a blouse or sweater fits.
blocks.a: No: slacks or a skirt with a blouse or sweater.

blocks.html: Reading "black tie optional" as "jeans are fine" or "business casual" as athletic wear. Dressing for the occasion is a way of showing respect for the host. When unsure, ask, or dress a step up.

Customs differ: what counts as formal varies by region and culture, and traditional dress from many cultures is correct formal wear. Climate matters too: a summer garden party is lighter than a winter dinner.
